Definition: from G3037 and a derivative of G4766; stone-strewed, i.e. a tessellated mosaic on which the Roman tribunal was placed:--Pavement.
BiblicalUsage: lithóstrōtos means Pavement — a small word with a sharp edge. In John 19:13, "and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Pavement is where the judgment seat sat — Pilate brought Jesus out, sat down, and handed Him over on a mosaic floor.
